resolved_findings.title: Put the negligible soundness term after the adversary quantifier
resolved_findings.original_detail: The current statement chooses one negligible mu before quantifying over every QPT prover. Computational hardness gives a negligible bound for each fixed efficient adversary, not a single pointwise bound for the union of all polynomial-time machines with unrestricted constants.
resolved_findings.rereview_detail: The revised 4F24 now correctly places mu_P after P, but asserts one mu_P for all x of length lambda while selecting advice-free uniform QPT as the default hardness model. A worst-case no-instance sequence x_lambda need not be efficiently generable and must be carried as polynomial classical advice in the LWE reduction. Explicitly adopt the advice-resistant LWE assumption already recorded in 4F15 (and compatible auxiliary-input security for the abstract primitives), or supply a justified uniformly generated input-family formulation. The mere absence of extra quantum input to P does not remove the nonuniform classical information in arbitrary x_lambda.
resolved_findings.resolution: Completeness has its own mu_c. Soundness fixes an efficient circuit and its parameter-dependent advice family before choosing mu_P. Revision 3 explicitly assumes advice-resistant LWE and the same advised security for adaptive-hardcore, injective-invariance and fixed-mask primitives, so the all-input statement no longer relies on advice-free uniform hardness.
resolved_findings.verification: BCMVV v4 Definition 2.5 explicitly includes parameter-dependent polynomial quantum advice. For a fixed prover/advice family, if the supremum of its soundness excess over length-lambda no instances were nonnegligible, a maximizing input sequence could be supplied as polynomial classical advice, independent of the fresh key. The stated stronger hardness assumption covers that reduction. No single negligible function is required for all efficient adversaries.

resolved_findings.title: Distinguish ideal square-root states from finite-gate implementations
resolved_findings.original_detail: 4F07 fixes a finite universal gate set, while 4F13 and 4F26 require exact output of the displayed Gaussian/uniform square-root amplitudes, including clean coherent control. Universality only gives approximation; for example the usual Clifford+T set does not exactly prepare a uniform state of odd support size. The cited Gaussian preparation argument uses numerical precision.
resolved_findings.resolution: Exact distributions and ideal square-root states are distinguished from finite-gate implementations. The preparation approximation includes coherent control, output, workspace and an arbitrary entangled reference, with ideal zero workspace. The negligible implementation error is accumulated separately from the f/f' Hellinger error.
resolved_findings.verification: Checked the joint norm formula for arbitrary v_0,v_1 and normalized control/reference input; branchwise probabilities alone are explicitly insufficient. Common-experiment stability follows from 4F28, and polynomial-call error is bounded by the hybrid triangle inequality. 4F16 no longer claims exact test acceptance for compiled states. This matches finite-precision preparation in BCMVV Section 4.3, equations (23)-(26), footnote 3.

source_ranges.range: Section 4.3, equations (23)-(26), footnote 3 on preparation to good precision

resolved_findings.title: Handle the certain-success endpoint in the repetition lemma
resolved_findings.original_detail: The honest-case assertion allows c=1, but D(a||c) is only given by a formula with denominator 1-c and no endpoint convention. Also the honest comparison should be explicitly a separate completeness case; under the preceding soundness assumption M<=sI no state of that same operator can have c>a>s.
resolved_findings.resolution: The no-instance operator M<=sI and the honest yes-instance operator M_yes are separated. The finite divergence formula has 0<a<c<1, and c=1 is handled directly with zero lower-tail failure probability.
resolved_findings.verification: Rechecked the tensor-product moment-generating bound for arbitrary entangled input, the positive Chernoff optimizer, D''=1/(a(1-a)), and the honest product-state lower tail. At c=1, Y_yes=k almost surely, so the event Y_yes<=ka is empty when a<1.

resolved_findings.title: Split the new odd-cycle obstruction from endpoint-dependent parity linearization
resolved_findings.original_detail: The revision adds a correct general theorem about derivatives of arbitrary binary functions on odd-order translation cycles. This theorem is independent of the original endpoint-dependent binary-secret linearization lemma, has a separate proof and different hypotheses, and is now a prerequisite used by 4F00, 4F24 and 4F29. Keeping both in the same permanent note violates the required one-question atomicity.
resolved_findings.resolution: The arbitrary-encoding odd-cycle obstruction and its complete proof are now the separate atomic theorem 4F2C. The endpoint-dependent linearization remains in 4F18. Obstruction links and prerequisite edges from 4F24/4F29 are retargeted, while 4F18's link is correctly treated as a further consequence rather than a prerequisite.
resolved_findings.verification: Read all of 4F2C. It introduces q,n,w,G,s,J,d,g and the orbit length locally; q may be any odd integer and J need not be injective. Minimal return time r divides q by Euclidean division; the mod-two sum of derivatives is zero, so an odd cycle cannot have every derivative equal to one. This includes s=0, d=0 and composite odd q. Independently checked 10,296 finite Boolean-function/translation cases as corroboration, not as the general proof.
